extracted.intended_audience: Organizations and administrators applying for or receiving SAMHSA grant funding (grant applicants, grantees, grants management staff).
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applying to, receiving, and managing SAMHSA grants including pre-award (NOFO/application), registration, compliance with federal regulations, post-award reporting and amendments, and block grant specifics. Intended to help applicants and recipients understand procedural and regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 2 CFR 200 and 2 CFR 300 (effective Oct 1, 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting October 1, 2025, all awards issued by SAMHSA will be subject to the applicable provisions of 2 CFR 200 and 2 CFR 300.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These federal regulations establish uniform administrative requirements, cost principles, and audit standards for federal awards, including those specific to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. Recipients are recommended to familiarize themselves with these regulations to ensure compliance moving forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of HHS PRWORA Notice and enforcement stay
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS has agreed to stay enforcement and application through September 10, 2025, of the item: 'Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 (PRWORA); Interpretation of 'Federal Public Benefit.''
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This stay period permits the agency to consider whether to provide additional information about the HHS PRWORA Notice. Applicants/recipients should be aware of current enforcement status and potential future changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow requirements and instructions in each NOFO
rubrics_metrics.description: SAMHSA announces grant funding opportunities through Notice of Funding Opportunities (NOFOs). Each NOFO contains all the information you need to apply for a grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must consult the specific NOFO for eligible activities, application instructions, deadlines, required forms, and evaluation criteria. The NOFO is the authoritative source for applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration with Grants.gov, SAM, and eRA Commons
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must use the applicable systems (Grants.gov, System for Award Management (SAM), eRA Commons) as part of the application and award process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A significant change has been made to the SAM registration process — applicants should refer to SAM FAQs. For technical questions about eRA Commons or issues submitting an application, contact SAMHSA as directed. Ensure registrations are current and completed well before deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Application Guide, Forms, and Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: SAMHSA provides an Application Guide and Forms and Resources to support NOFO submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Application Guide and required forms to prepare applications that meet format, content, and submission requirements. Use provided resources (Forms, Terms Tracking, Submitting Additional Materials) to avoid submission errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation Guidelines for Individuals with Lived Experience and Family
rubrics_metrics.description: SAMHSA offers specific guidance for participation of individuals with lived experience and family in grant-related activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the participation guidelines when including individuals with lived experience or family members in program design, implementation, or advisory roles as specified in relevant resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the Grant Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: SAMHSA provides information on how grants are reviewed as part of the application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should familiarize themselves with the grant review process to understand evaluation criteria, reviewer expectations, and how proposed projects will be assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants Oversight and Compliance expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: In the post-award phase, the agency collaborates with the grantee to ensure progress on SAMHSA-supported programs while minimizing risks to Federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are subject to oversight; maintain documentation, follow award terms, and respond to monitoring and audit requests to demonstrate proper use of funds and program performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Award (NoA) is authoritative post-award document
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Award (NoA) is the official document issued to grant recipients after an award is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the NoA carefully for award terms, budget, performance period, conditions, and reporting requirements. The NoA establishes the official grant obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant recipients must meet specified reporting requirements for SAMHSA awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow required financial, performance, and other reports (frequency, formats, and submission channels) as stated in the NOFO and NoA to remain compliant and to facilitate continued funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post Award Amendments and related applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes exist for submitting post-award amendments to awards when changes are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Post Award Amendment Applications and related procedures to request changes to scope, budget, or other award terms. Follow instructions and obtain approvals before implementing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation Grants / Submitting Non-Competing Continuation Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: There are procedures for continuation funding (non-competing continuation applications) to extend multi-year projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit non-competing continuation applications per the prescribed timeline and required documentation to request continuation funding; follow guidance in Forms and Resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Closeout requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must follow closeout procedures at the end of the award period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete required final reports, reconcile financials, retain records, and meet any other closeout conditions specified in the NoA and SAMHSA guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of GPRA Measurement Tools
rubrics_metrics.description: SAMHSA references GPRA measurement tools for program performance measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement required performance measurement and data collection tools (e.g., GPRA) as specified to report outcomes and meet federal performance reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to Policies and Regulations cited by SAMHSA
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant recipients must adhere to applicable policies and regulations referenced by SAMHSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult SAMHSA policies and federal regulations (including executive orders where applicable) to ensure award management, compliance, and reporting meet legal and agency standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow prescribed submission channels and tracking tools
rubrics_metrics.description: SAMHSA points applicants to specific channels and tools (Grants.gov, eRA Commons, Terms Tracking, Submitting Additional Materials) for submissions and tracking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the designated submission platforms and tracking systems to submit applications, amendments, continuation requests, and additional materials. Failure to use required channels may delay or disqualify submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain cybersecurity and protect Federal funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal financial assistance award recipients play a crucial part in safeguarding Federal funds and maintaining a secure cyber environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should follow cybersecurity best practices and check resources such as the Grants.gov blog post referenced for guidance on protecting systems and data related to grant administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Block grant characteristics and application path
rubrics_metrics.description: A block grant is a noncompetitive, formula grant mandated by the U.S. Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For block grants (e.g., Community Mental Health Services Block Grant (MHBG), Substance Use Prevention, Treatment, and Recovery Services Block Grant (SUBG)), consult the specific Block Grant Application guidance; these grants follow formula allocation rather than competitive NOFO processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact points for questions and technical issues
rubrics_metrics.description: SAMHSA provides contact information for questions about grant announcements, submission issues, or technical questions about eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have questions about a NOFO, problems submitting an application, or other technical issues, contact the agency as directed in the NOFO or on the Grants pages to get assistance and avoid missed deadlines.
